# GarageAI

> GarageAI (also written Garage AI) is a two-sided marketplace for local AI inference in Europe. Garage owners ("operators") connect GPUs they already own and get paid per token for the requests they serve; buyers use open models through one OpenAI-compatible API. The principle: Europe's AI capacity can come from hardware people and companies already own, not only from hyperscaler data centres.

## Key facts (what works today)

- **For buyers:** Sign up at https://app.garageai.eu, create an API key and call the OpenAI-compatible API at https://api.garageai.eu/v1 (works with OpenAI SDKs, agents and coding tools), or use the chat in the portal. Pay per token with prepaid credits (card via Stripe).
- **Pricing:** Each garage sets its own price per million tokens (input and output); GarageAI has no price list of its own. Buyers pay per token at the price of the garage that served the request; cached input is billed at the garage's lower cache-read price.
- **Two ways to buy a model:** "Specific garage" (a named garage, e.g. for location; you pay its price) or "Pool" (one model name across every garage offering the model; each request goes to one healthy garage and is billed at that garage's price, with automatic failover). Both are shared, not exclusive, capacity.
- **For operators:** Sign in at https://app.garageai.eu/connect ("Connect this computer") and run one line on the GPU machine: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/magnusfroste/garageai/main/cli/install.sh | sh -s -- connect` (no secrets in it). Requirements: a Mac (Apple silicon) or Linux machine with a GPU and a runtime running with a model loaded. Windows is coming soon; until then there is a beta PowerShell connect script for Ollama and LM Studio (https://github.com/magnusfroste/garageai/blob/main/scripts/garageai-connect.ps1), tested in CI but not yet on a real GPU machine, shown in the portal only as legacy instructions; beta testers can email powerup@garageai.eu with the subject "Windows beta". Supported runtimes: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang and Paddock (beta). The line installs GarageAI Bridge (`garageai`, open source, in beta) and connects the garage in a few minutes: the operator confirms the machine in the browser (no token is copied), Bridge opens its own encrypted WireGuard tunnel to the gateway (no VPN app; the runtime stays on localhost), checks the runtime and registers the models, and a heartbeat service keeps the models and their context windows in sync. Every model must pass an automated acceptance test (time-to-first-token, tokens/second) before it can be sold.
- **Operator earnings:** Operators set their own price and earn it for every token their garage serves, also for pool requests. No platform fee during launch (a fee will come later). Wallet and payouts are being built.
- **Technology (open source):** GarageAI Bridge carries a WireGuard tunnel in user space from the garage out to a hub on the gateway — no inbound ports, no VPN app, the runtime stays on localhost, garages can only answer the gateway and cannot reach each other. A self-hosted NetBird mesh is the fallback for networks that block UDP. LiteLLM gateway (OpenAI-compatible API, routing, failover, usage metering) on an EU VPS (Hetzner, Helsinki). The gateway does not reveal to buyers which garage served a request, and it automatically blocks clients that guess API keys or probe it.
- **Privacy, honestly:** Traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS to the gateway, WireGuard to the garage), but prompts are processed on the operator's machine. Verified garages and data-processing agreements are planned before selling to buyers with sensitive data.
- **GarageAI Bridge:** how a garage connects since October 2026 (macOS and Linux). Commands: `garageai connect`, `garageai doctor` (what runs on the machine, what is wrong and how to fix it), `garageai uninstall`, and `garageai mcp` (read-only checks and a troubleshooting guide for the operator's own AI agent). It never reports prompts, keys or command lines. Bridge updates itself to the current stable release; `garageai pause` takes a garage off the market for a while; the tunnel passes only inference requests to the runtime. Planned: automatic pause when the owner games, GarageAI Smart (models in demand downloaded for the garage, Ollama), and a local control panel. Roadmap: https://github.com/magnusfroste/garageai/blob/main/docs/bridge.md
- **Status:** Launched in 2026 after a private beta in spring 2026. Live, with the first garages serving open models.
- **License:** Open source, MIT.

## Vision (not today's product)

Garage nodes running largely on locally produced energy (rooftop solar, home batteries, EV batteries), many more garages across Europe, and larger regional clusters.
